chapter: Hopkins, Kelly's Stables and Red Allen
title: His love of recording and spontaneous studio sessions
summary: Clarke made countless records and liked the on-the-spot thrill of sessions, as when Miles, J.J., Monk and Milt walked in not knowing what to play.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And so -- and you know, I haven't asked you, but I feel -- I know full well that you were making a lot of records all these different times, weren't you?
Yes. When I -- well, I figured it out. I said I've made so many jazz records that I can't keep up with
Yeah. And I didn't care who I recorded with, you know.
You know? It was like a new toy.
Creating music, and you never know how it's going to come out, and --
And so often, you know, you'll get some wonderful results.
It's the thing of sitting down with different guys.
That's right. That's right. On the spot recording.
You know, because I'm a person, I like to do things like they should -- like to rehearse correctly.
Because I came up through all the rehearsing and doing things correct.
So to do things on the spot, it kind of appealed to me too, as being something different.

Like we'd walk in the studio with Miles, and we'd have Miles, J.J. and Monk and Milt and we'd all walk in the studio and then Miles would say, 'What are we going to play?' And then right away something would come up in my stomach. It was such a thrill, you know. I said no-one knows what we're going to play. Now, what's going to happen?
But fortunately the things we did turned out very well.
Well, the thing was that all -- I mean
You know, like we talked last night about the time element.
I mean something has happened and everything was right brewing at that time and things were all happening.
It couldn't happen any other way.
That's right. It's the first time you've mentioned Miles. Did he used to come in, down and hear you? When did you first meet Miles?
Oh, Miles came -- well, I met Miles really in St. Louis when I was there with Dizzy's band, right after the war.
Oh, well then -- don't -- we won't jump ahead on ourselves.
Hold it. We'll come back to that, then.

But those -- so the record sessions you were making then -- just one second -- well, did you make some -- did you make some sessions and -- you and Monk, then? Or that's hard to remember back, whether you did or not.
I didn't record with Monk really until after I was demobilized.
Yeah. Well, okay, let's not talk about the records yet, because that wasn't the heyday for record time, really, was it?
